original_title: Cleaning an IBM 5150, And The Perfect Period PCB Soldermask
original_content:
Now that early PCs have moved firmly from the realm of e-waste into being collectors items, its worth putting in some effort to restore them if you find one. [Epictronics] has an early IBM 5150, the ancestor of all todays PCs, and is bringing it back to life. Along the way, hes building a replica AdLib sound card, making a useful discovery about how to make new parts look authentic.
The video below the break is a gentle journey through an early PC teardown, followed by the construction of the replica sound card. Heres the interesting nugget of information: these new cards are careful recreations of the originals, but they just dont look right. It seems modern soldermask is too shiny, and as luck would have it, theres another option that is much more period-authentic. We hadnt noticed matte green was available, but it certainly captures the look of those days much better.
As you might expect, such an old machine has a range of dead capacitors and a few chips. Theres a lucky escape with a Varta battery on an expansion card, having very little leakage, and part of one of the floppy drives needs some surgery. Its gentle hacking thats engaging to watch, and of course, at the end, were rewarded with the thing booting properly.
You might think reproducing a sound card is unusual, but weve seen it a number of times.
